name: Stripe
summary: Stripe builds payments and financial infrastructure for internet businesses. Its APIs handle online payments, billing, fraud prevention and money movement for companies of every size.
hiring_signals: Regularly hires backend, infrastructure and reliability engineers.
talking_points: How they keep payment APIs backward compatible for years
Running reliability at their transaction volume
Where Billing and usage-based pricing are heading

name: Notion
summary: Notion makes a connected workspace for notes, docs, wikis and project tracking. Teams use it to keep knowledge and planning in one place, with AI features built in.
hiring_signals: Hiring across product engineering, AI and design.
talking_points: How they built the block-based editor
Scaling a real-time collaborative data model
How Notion AI is used inside teams

name: Ramp
summary: Ramp offers corporate cards and spend management software for finance teams. It automates expenses, bill payments and accounting so companies spend less time on paperwork.
hiring_signals: Fast-growing engineering team; often hiring full-stack and backend engineers.
talking_points: Using AI to automate expense review

name: Datadog
summary: Datadog is a monitoring and security platform for cloud applications. It brings metrics, traces, logs and security signals together so engineering teams can see and fix problems fast.
hiring_signals: Hiring backend, distributed systems and site reliability engineers.
talking_points: Ingesting trillions of data points a day
How they think about observability costs
The overlap of observability and security

name: Cloudflare
summary: Cloudflare runs a global network that makes websites and apps faster and more secure. It offers CDN, DDoS protection, zero trust networking and a developer platform at the edge.
hiring_signals: Hiring systems, networking and edge platform engineers.
talking_points: Building on Workers at the edge
How they mitigate record DDoS attacks

name: Vercel
summary: Vercel is a cloud platform for building and deploying web applications, and the company behind Next.js. It focuses on frontend developer experience and fast global delivery.
hiring_signals: Hiring frontend, platform and developer relations roles.

name: Figma
summary: Figma is a collaborative design tool that runs in the browser. Designers, engineers and product teams use it to design, prototype and hand off interfaces together.
hiring_signals: Hiring product engineers, graphics and infrastructure engineers.
talking_points: Rendering a design tool in the browser with WebAssembly

name: Databricks
summary: Databricks provides a data and AI platform built around the lakehouse architecture. Companies use it to store, process and analyze data and to train and serve machine learning models.
hiring_signals: Hiring data infrastructure, distributed systems and ML engineers.
talking_points: Open source projects like Delta Lake and MLflow

name: Snowflake
summary: Snowflake is a cloud data platform for storing, sharing and analyzing data. It separates storage and compute so teams can scale analytics workloads independently.
hiring_signals: Hiring database, query engine and data engineering roles.
talking_points: Running AI next to the data with Cortex

name: MongoDB
summary: MongoDB makes a document database and the Atlas cloud database service. Developers use it to build applications with flexible schemas, search and vector search.
hiring_signals: Hiring database engineers, cloud and developer experience roles.

name: Twilio
summary: Twilio provides communication APIs for SMS, voice, video and email. Businesses use it to build customer messaging, verification and contact center experiences.

name: Supabase
summary: Supabase is an open source backend platform built on Postgres. It gives developers a database, authentication, storage, realtime and edge functions in one project.
hiring_signals: Fully remote team; hires open source and Postgres engineers.
talking_points: Building a business on open source Postgres
Row level security as an auth model

name: Linear
summary: Linear makes issue tracking and project planning software for product teams. It is known for speed, keyboard-first design and an opinionated workflow.
hiring_signals: Small, selective team; hires senior product engineers and designers.
talking_points: Keeping a small team while growing

name: Apple
summary: Apple designs consumer hardware, software and services including iPhone, Mac and the App Store. It hires across silicon, operating systems, machine learning and services.
hiring_signals: Large, steady hiring across hardware, software and ML.
talking_points: Apple Silicon and performance per watt

name: Hugging Face
summary: Hugging Face hosts open machine learning models, datasets and demos, and maintains popular libraries like Transformers. It is a central hub for the open source AI community.
hiring_signals: Remote-friendly; hires ML engineers and open source maintainers.
talking_points: How Spaces grew into a demo platform
